name: PostgreSQL
desc: The default serious database: transactions, JSON, extensions, full text. Use unless you have a specific reason not to.

name: MySQL
desc: Ubiquitous relational database with cheap hosting everywhere. Use for WordPress, legacy apps and PlanetScale.

name: SQLite
desc: The whole database is one file in your process. Use for local apps, tests and single-server deployments.

name: MariaDB
desc: Community fork of MySQL with extra engines. Use when you want MySQL compatibility under a freer licence.

name: SQL Server
desc: Microsoft relational database with deep .NET and Power BI integration. Use in Microsoft-centric enterprises.

name: CockroachDB
desc: Distributed Postgres-compatible SQL that survives node loss. Use when multi-region writes and uptime are contractual.

name: Neon
desc: Serverless Postgres that scales to zero and branches like git. Use for preview environments per pull request.

name: PlanetScale
desc: Vitess-backed MySQL with safe online schema changes. Use when migrations on a huge table must not lock it.

name: Turso
desc: SQLite replicated to the edge, one database per tenant if you want. Use for read-heavy globally distributed apps.

name: MongoDB
desc: Document store with flexible schemas. Use when the shape of your data genuinely varies per record.

name: DynamoDB
desc: AWS key-value store with single-digit millisecond reads at any scale. Use when access patterns are known and fixed.

name: Cassandra
desc: Wide-column store built for enormous write volume. Use for time series and event logs at petabyte scale.

name: CouchDB
desc: Document database built around replication and offline sync. Use for apps that must work with no network.

name: Redis
desc: In-memory key-value store with lists, sets and pub/sub. Use for caching, sessions, rate limits and job queues.

name: Valkey
desc: Linux Foundation fork of Redis after the licence change. Use when the licence matters to your legal team.

name: Memcached
desc: Pure in-memory cache, nothing else. Use when you need a cache and refuse the temptation to store state in it.

name: Upstash
desc: Serverless Redis and Kafka billed per request over HTTP. Use from edge functions that cannot hold a TCP connection.

name: Elasticsearch
desc: Distributed search and analytics engine. Use for log analysis and search over very large corpora.

name: Meilisearch
desc: Typo-tolerant instant search you can self-host in minutes. Use when Elasticsearch is far more than you need.

name: Typesense
desc: Fast open-source search with simple defaults. Use as a self-hosted Algolia alternative.

name: Algolia
desc: Hosted search-as-you-type with ranking tuned for you. Use for storefronts and docs where relevance sells.

name: Prisma
desc: Typed ORM with a declarative schema and generated migrations. Use when you want your database shape in version control.

name: Drizzle
desc: Typed SQL query builder with no runtime engine. Use when you want Prisma safety but SQL that reads like SQL.

name: TypeORM
desc: Decorator-based ORM common in NestJS projects. Use when the framework you picked already assumes it.

name: Kysely
desc: Type-safe query builder, no schema DSL. Use when you want autocomplete over a database you already own.

name: SQLAlchemy
desc: The Python ORM and Core query layer. Use in any serious Python service that touches SQL.

name: Snowflake
desc: Cloud warehouse separating storage from compute. Use when analysts need heavy SQL without touching production.

name: BigQuery
desc: Serverless warehouse billed per byte scanned. Use for huge ad-hoc analytical queries on GCP.

name: Databricks
desc: Lakehouse platform over Spark and Delta Lake. Use when data engineering and ML share one pipeline.

name: ClickHouse
desc: Column store that aggregates billions of rows in milliseconds. Use for product analytics and observability backends.

name: DuckDB
desc: In-process analytical database that queries Parquet and CSV directly. Use for local analysis without a warehouse bill.

name: dbt
desc: Version-controlled SQL transformations with tests and lineage. Use to turn raw warehouse tables into trusted models.

name: pgvector
desc: Vector similarity search as a Postgres extension. Use when you already run Postgres and refuse a second database.

name: Pinecone
desc: Fully managed vector database. Use when you want RAG retrieval working without operating an index.

name: Qdrant
desc: Open-source vector search with rich payload filtering. Use when metadata filters matter as much as similarity.

name: Weaviate
desc: Vector database with built-in vectoriser modules and hybrid search. Use when you want embeddings generated for you.

name: Chroma
desc: Embedded vector store that runs in your Python process. Use for prototypes and notebooks before you need a server.

name: Amazon S3
desc: The object storage everything else imitates. Use for uploads, backups and static assets.

name: Cloudflare R2
desc: S3-compatible storage with no egress fees. Use when users download far more than they upload.

name: MinIO
desc: S3-compatible object storage you run yourself. Use on-premise or in air-gapped environments.

name: Cloud Storage
desc: Google object storage with tiered classes. Use when the stack already lives on GCP.
